description:
FILED s446i (Opus agent I), from the #513 probes.

REPRODUCER:

    open(my $c, '>', $file) or die; print $c "hello\n"; close $c;
    open(my $f, '+<', $file) or die;
    my $r = open(my $dup, '+<&', $f);
    print "ret:", (defined $r ? ($r?1:0) : "undef"), "\n";
    if ($r) { my $l = <$dup>; print "read:[$l]" }
        perl  ret:1   read:[hello\n]
        PCL   warning: Unknown open mode: +<&      ret:undef

CORPUS SITE: perl-tests/scalar.t:84 `open my $dup,'+<&',$fh;` (and perl's own
t/op/scalar.t).

CAUSE: %p-open-impl dispatches the dup path on
`(member mode-str '(">&" "<&" ">&=" "<&="))`, so the four `+`-prefixed
read-write spellings fall to the `(t (warn "Unknown open mode: ~A"))` arm.

SHAPE OF A FIX (small, and s446i deliberately did NOT take it to keep its own
change reviewable): add the four modes to that member list, and make
%p-open-dup's direction dispatch three-valued instead of
`(if (char= (char mode-str 0) #\>) :output :input)` -- a leading `+` means an
:io fd-stream (`:input t :output t`).  The source resolution is already shared
(s446i routed it through %p-resolve-fh).

BAR: the reproducer + `+>&` + both `=` forms + a write-then-read through the
dup + the scalar.t row; a Pl/t guard row in print-fh-magic-01.t beside the
s446i dup rows; the full sweep (a cl/ change) with scalar.t read row by row.

--- DONE s448n (Opus round-6 agent N), commit efa5555 ---

Fixed, and the fix is BIGGER than the task described, because the TWO-argument
form was a second, SILENT half: %p-open-parse-2arg's `+<` and `+>` arms sit
above the dup arms and are PREFIXES of `+<&` / `+>&`, so `open FH, "+>&SRC"`
parsed as mode `+>` on a file literally named `&SRC` -- and CREATED it (probed;
the stray file is real).  The four hand-written dup arms are now one
longest-first prefix scan over `+p-open-dup-modes+`, the ONE list %p-open-impl's
dispatch also reads.

%p-open-dup's direction test became `%p-dup-make-stream`: `+` -> bidirectional,
`>` -> output, `<` -> input, explicit error otherwise (rule 12 -- the only thing
that can catch the two sites disagreeing about the mode set).

Probed 5.40.3 (all identical after): four `+` spellings open and read; `&` dup
gets a NEW fd, `&=` fdopen shares the source's; `+>&` does NOT truncate; the dup
is writable and its writes land in the source's file; 3-arg by fd NUMBER works;
2-arg `+<&SRC`/`+>&SRC` read the source and leave no stray file.

Guard Pl/t/print-fh-magic-01.t 18 -> 21 rows.  Gate 177/6000 PASS.
perl-tests/scalar.t 84/32 -> 86/30 (the in-memory `+<&` dup pair at
scalar.t:87-88 -- both rows have EMPTY descriptions, which is why the
fail-baseline never listed them).  Sweep-baseline movement for the merge review:
pass-baseline `scalar.t OK 84 32 128` -> `86 30 128`; fail-baseline rows
`scalar.t [perl #40267] - Bad file descriptor` and `scalar.t Bad file
descriptor` change DESCRIPTION (to `[perl #40267] - ` and the empty string) --
those descriptions interpolate `$!`, which used to be the stale EBADF the FAILED
`+<&` dup left behind.  Both rows fail before and after; only the text moved.

Residue filed: #590 (write to a dup of a read-only fd claims success, then
aborts at close), #591 (a dup does not sync the source's buffered read position
-- the dup starts at EOF).  Both PRE-EXISTING, both visible on the untouched
`>&`/`<&` modes.
subject: The READ-WRITE dup modes `+<&` / `+>&` (and their `=` forms) are not in %p-open-impl's dup list -- `open my $dup, "+<&", $fh` warns "Unknown open mode" and returns undef where perl dups (perl-tests/scalar.t:84)
